title: GALEX shows that the UV excess of extreme 12 um excess field dwarfs comes from blended hot sources, not activity; activity tests find no youth signal in 93 dust dimmers but have low power
abstract: Question: are main-sequence dust dimmers and extreme-dust field dwarfs young or magnetically active? Prior campaign ages came only from kinematics. Approach: 93 dimmers (81 ZTF dippers of Tzanidakis et al. 2025 and 12 campaign dimmers), 951 Gaia DR3 dwarfs with a confirmed extreme 12 um excess, and 645 Praesepe members (0.7 Gyr, positive control) were compared with 18,976 matched Gaia field controls. Indicators: GALEX NUV and FUV detection and NUV-G, eROSITA eRASS1 coronal detection, and the Gaia DR3 rotational-modulation table. We also tested if GALEX and AllWISE centroids move away from the star in the same direction. Results: Praesepe gives X-ray and rotation odds ratios of 2.5 (1.7-3.5) and 2.4 (1.4-3.7); NUV is weak (1.7). The 12 um excess stars have a strong UV excess (NUV odds ratio 5.8; FUV 181 detections against 6.5 expected), but no X-ray (0.70, 0.17-1.9) or rotation (0.97, 0.30-2.3) excess. Their GALEX and WISE offsets align (mean cos 0.36 against 0.04 for controls; 0.63 for FUV-detected stars, with the UV centroid 0.9 arcsec along the WISE offset), and FUV-NUV is near 1 mag. Thus the UV excess comes from blended hot background sources, not activity. FUV flags find blends in the WISE-centred class and reduce the unblended bound from 197 to 181 stars. The dimmers show no activity excess in any indicator (NUV rank z = 1.4; 0 X-ray and 0 rotation detections), but at their 1.2 kpc median distance these tests have low power. Limitations: no images or spectra of the blend sources; shallow eRASS1; NUV cannot detect a 0.7 Gyr age. GALEX NUV and AllWISE centroid offsets of 12 um excess stars point in the same direction, most strongly for FUV-detected stars; controls show no alignment.
NUV-G and FUV-NUV colours: excess stars are bluer than the field locus and hot in FUV-NUV; detected dust dimmers lie on the field locus.
